title: Brooks Lab Western Blotting Protocol
author: Brooks Lab University of California
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcsmiwc6
materials: Before use, thaw and add 1 tablet of protease inhibitor (PI) per 10 ml aliquot . (Roche cOmplete ™ , Mini Protease Inhibitor Cocktail).

Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit #23225 or #23227, Thermo Sci with 2 mg/ml BSA standard. Use instructions from kit. Equilibrate reagents, samples, and standards to Room temperature . Use the Microplate reader instructions.
Prepare the following solutions for SDS-PAGE, Transfer, and Antibody Incubations:
Export report as an excel doc.

steps.title: Prepare RIPA buffer
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL RIPA without protease inhibitors, aliquot into 10 mL portions, cover and freeze at –20 °C, or use pre‑made Pierce RIPA (100 mL, aliquoted 10 mL, stored –20 °C).

steps.title: Harvest cells on ice
steps.instruction: Keep all reagents on ice. Wash a confluent 10 cm plate of cells twice with ice‑cold PBS, add 1 mL cold RIPA containing protease inhibitors, scrape cells, transfer to a pre‑chilled 2 mL tube on ice.

steps.title: Lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate on ice for 20 seconds, vortexing periodically.

steps.title: Clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Spin at maximum speed in a refrigerated (4 °C) microcentrifuge for 10 seconds, transfer the supernatant to a clean LoBind 1.5 mL tube, aliquot ~200 µL each, and store aliquots at –80 °C. (Optional: perform additional sonication for nucleic‑acid removal – see next step.)

steps.title: Retrieve sonicator adaptor
steps.instruction: Bring a timer, ear‑cuffs, on‑ice samples, and a balance to the second‑floor Kamakaka Lab to obtain the plastic tube adaptor (back of second drawer in the second bay from the back).

steps.title: Set up sonicator
steps.instruction: In the cold‑room sonicator, place the outflow tube on the shelf, fill the glass water reservoir to the top of the white line, set timer on hold, select max setting (10), constant mode, then flip on.

steps.title: Sonicate lysates
steps.instruction: Hold the tubes in the adaptor within the water bath for 30 seconds, then place tubes on ice for 1 minute; repeat the 30‑second sonication for a total of two 30‑second bursts.

steps.title: Prepare BSA standards
steps.instruction: From a 2 mg/mL BSA stock vial, prepare a dilution series covering 20 µg/mL to 2000 µg/mL for the standard curve.

steps.title: Prepare working reagent
steps.instruction: Make a fresh 50:1 (A:B) working reagent, enough for all standards, unknowns and three replicates each.

steps.title: Run BCA assay
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of each unknown or standard to a 96‑well plate well, add 200 µL of the working reagent with a 200 µL pipettor, mix gently, cover with foil, incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes in a shaking incubator (gentle shaking), then cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Measure absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 562 nm on a VarioSkan, plot the standard curve in the Skanit software, and calculate protein concentrations of the unknowns.

steps.title: Make 1× Laemmli buffer (MLB)
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, add 100 µL 2‑mercaptoethanol to 900 µL 4× Laemmli sample buffer to obtain 1× MLB.

steps.title: Dilute samples with MLB
steps.instruction: Dilute each sample at a 3:1 ratio (sample:MLB); for a 30 µL final volume add 7.5 µL MLB to 22.5 µL sample (still in RIPA) in a 1.5 mL LoBind safety‑lock tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Pre‑wet PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Soak the PVDF membrane from the Bio‑Rad Trans‑Blot kit first in 190‑proof ethanol, then in 1× transfer buffer.

steps.title: Prepare transfer stack
steps.instruction: Pre‑soak blotting stacks in 1× transfer buffer (per bottle directions), then layer in the Trans‑Blot drawer: first stack, membrane, gel, second stack; roll out bubbles gently with a conical tube.

steps.title: Run protein transfer
steps.instruction: Run the transfer on the Bio‑Rad system using a standard Mini‑Gel TGX at 25 mA, 25 V for 3 minutes. While running, pour 5 % milk in 1× PBST directly into the cleaned small black Western‑blot box.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the transferred blot for 1 hour at room temperature in 5 % milk in 1× PBST, then photograph the blot to record orientation.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation (β‑Actin)
steps.instruction: Add primary β‑actin antibody (sc‑47778) diluted 1:500 in 5 % milk/PBST to the blot, cover, and incubate overnight in the cold room on an orbital shaker, covered with plastic.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash the blot 3 times with 1× PBST for up to 10 minutes total.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody at 1:10 000 (2 µL secondary in 20 mL 5 % milk/PBST), add to the blot, and incubate 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Discard secondary solution and wash the blot 3 times for 5 minutes each in 1× PBST.

steps.title: ECL development
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL of each ECL reagent in a 15 mL conical tube, apply the mixture to the blot, incubate 5 minutes while shaking occasionally by hand, covered.

steps.title: Image chemiluminescence
steps.instruction: Drain the blot, place it between plastic sheets, and image using the Bio‑Rad GelDoc (or ChemiDoc XRS+). After imaging, the blot can be re‑probed for actin without stripping, using anti‑actin‑HRP as described later.

steps.title: Prepare gel for electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Remove the gel from its package, peel off the green strip at the bottom, rinse each well three times with ~1 mL running buffer (using a 1 mL pipettor).

steps.title: Assemble gel chamber
steps.instruction: Place the gel with the tall plate facing out on one side of the holder, position the reservoir block opposite to create a running‑buffer reservoir, insert the second gel holder to fill the space, fill the chamber to the 2‑gel mark, verify no leaks, then test the circuit by turning on power to 70 V and checking for bubbles.

steps.title: Load samples and ladder
steps.instruction: Using a 20 µL conical‑tip pipettor, load 30 µL of each MLB‑diluted sample and 10 µL of Bio‑Rad Precision Plus Dual‑Color protein ladder into the gel wells.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 100–120 V (depending on desired resolution) until the ladder bands have separated to the regions of interest.

steps.title: Document gel orientation
steps.instruction: Photograph the gel with a phone after the run to record orientation.

steps.title: Block gel after transfer (repeat)
steps.instruction: Drain the milk block from the blot and add primary antibody (in milk block) as described in step 17; incubate overnight in the cold room as before.

steps.title: Actin loading‑control primary
steps.instruction: Incubate the blot for 20 minutes at room temperature with anti‑actin‑HRP primary antibody diluted 1:500 in 5 % milk block.

steps.title: Wash after actin primary
steps.instruction: Wash the blot 2–3 times with 1× PBST, 5 minutes each wash.

steps.title: Actin ECL detection
steps.instruction: Incubate the blot in ECL solution as in step 20 (5 minutes, occasional hand shaking, covered) and image.

steps.title: Prepare imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Place the blot on a white screen, insert the screen into the chamber drawer, and select a new protocol → blot → chem‑hi‑sensitivity → live‑focus setting in the Bio‑Rad software.

steps.title: Set acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Under Applications, choose chemidoc hi‑sensitivity, note image size, set gain to 2×, binning to 2 × 2; under Live Acquire, set range = 1, exposure = 600, total acquisitions = 100 (can be lowered for longer exposure), start time = 0.25 s for high‑expression targets.

steps.title: Save and document images
steps.instruction: Freeze and save each image as it appears. Without moving the blot, take a picture of the protein‑standard lanes by selecting Custom under Applications and creating an epi‑illumination protocol with the same gain and binning (verify image‑size prediction).

steps.title: Merge target and standard images
steps.instruction: Merge the target‑band image and the protein‑standard picture in Image Lab software using Image Tools. Store imaged blots at 4 °C in PBST for future stripping/re‑probing, or freeze flat at –20 °C in a plastic bag.
